problem: Suppose that $f(x,y)=(3-x){y}^{2}.$ Which of the following shaded areas gives the solution to the inequality $f(x,y)<0?$
worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=3$ and $y=0.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below. Since we have a strict inequality, we use dashed lines to divide the plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14052876/assets/e4d289aef282e076b062aab6d8f0f209396313e2c6403b2e27d1c0272ac90795.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14052876/assets/4cef3532a8e70098c030f2341800f06e9e54e4074126a0a97aecdf1f1c5185d0.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $(3-x)$ | ${y}^{2}$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-left | $(2,1)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Top-Right | $(4,1)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(2,-1)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(4,-1)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |

 

Finally, on our diagram, we shade in the solutions to $f(x,y)<0$ using the *last* column of the table above.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14052876/assets/c9ed172c5746b1b0afd2d9b7b3bbb21245115df164bfb7e34f4f530887376e28.png)
